title: fix(android): keep Gateway picker open while scrolling
body:
## What Problem This Solves Fixes: Android's Gateway picker closes when a finger swipe reaches or starts at the top of its saved-Gateway list. ## User Impact Users can scroll the picker without dismissing it or changing Gateways. Back, outside-tap dismissal, and the explicit accessibility dismiss action remain available. Gateway-scoped drafts and attachments, native-window ownership, and terminal lifecycle revocation are unchanged. The installed API-36 app now passes the native touch/IME/lifecycle test. The earlier Robolectric captures remain labeled separately. ## Why This Change Was Made Material 3's default nested-scroll/drag handling takes unconsumed list movement and settles the sheet to `Hidden`. The original touch reproduction invoked Material's `onDismissRequest`; temporary diagnostics showed no fold-owner rejection. This change disables sheet gestures only for the Gateway picker and preserves the existing handle's explicit accessibility dismissal action, which Material otherwise removes with gestures disabled. The picker, `FoldAwareSheet`, registry, and connection/draft owners are not replaced. There are no timers, automatic reopening, or relaxed lifecycle checks. Current iOS uses a native Menu/inline Picker; its separate draft policy is intentionally not copied to Android. Related open Android Gateway PRs did not implement this gesture fix. ## Evidence - **CI:** [exact-head run 36332834754](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36332834754) **passed**: 10 executed jobs, including both phone test variants, Wear, Ktlint, both native Access page-size lanes and `openclaw/ci-gate` (31 inapplicable jobs skipped). - **Sweeper:** [review of this exact head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159744#issuecomment-5857328480), completed 2026-09-27 at 16:27 UTC: **no findings**, prior registry-state finding addressed, **Ready for maintainer review (5/6)**. Repository-native review freshness gate passed. Sweeper inspected still images; it did not inspect the video, which was separately decoded, inspected, and verified to load in the PR by the author. Verified published head: `ee0d321443f027239a926b19877741a4bfc5bb1b`. - **Red → green:** the original `a67c5aac31375417320964c99bdcc5eefba6c056` fails after an actual `performTouchInput { swipeDown() }`: the picker disappears. The candidate passes downward overscroll at the start, upward scrolling into the list, both directions in the middle, and unchanged focused Gateway. Scroll-position assertions only observe results; they do not perform the interaction. - **31 tests passed:** `SidebarGatewayPickerTest` (26, 25.351 s) and `FoldAwareSheetTest` (5, 2.656 s), including search/IME insets, 1.5×/2× text, fold-safe geometry, explicit Back/accessibility dismissal, remount revocation, and retained per-owner drafts/attachments. The combined Gradle test/build invocation took 57 s. A subsequent strengthened touch-only run passed in 7.368 s. - **Build/checks:** `:app:assembleThirdPartyDebug`, `:app:assembleThirdPartyDebugAndroidTest`, `:app:ktlintCheck`, `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- `, and `git diff --check` passed. - **Review:** diff-scoped Deslop completed; fresh independent Codex AutoReview of the staged repaired candidate was `scoped-clean` at P0–P2, with no findings. - **Native red → green:** same API-36 emulator, 480×800 dark theme, 30 identical synthetic Gateways, and the same UiDevice driver. Reverting only `SidebarGatewayControl.kt` to its original `a67c5aac…` source fails at the first downward swipe in **9.537 s**; the picker disappears. The candidate completes successfully. - **Installed Android:** `SidebarGatewayTouchTest` passed in **22.613 s** on the configured Blacksmith Testbox (API 36, KVM, 480×800), using `adb shell am instrument -w -r -e class ai.openclaw.app.ui.SidebarGatewayTouchTest ai.openclaw.app.debug.test/androidx.test.runner.AndroidJUnitRunner`. Verified built/installed APK SHA equality and candidate source tree `f192c326f35aa2f27dc77e1f811485473e1746c5`. This is the dedicated manual instrumentation lane; per-PR native-access CI exercises a different class. It covers actual UiDevice finger swipes, unchanged focused Gateway, search with real Gboard, two-stage Back, and actual STOPPED/resume revocation. A separate `ChatComposerFeedbackTest` invocation passed first (5.253 s), leaving the same persisted Gateway ID; the picker test restores entries, active ID and ordered connections exactly. [Testbox workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36330823631); the command receipt is exit 0 (the lease workflow may show cancelled after normal cleanup). - **Fixture repairs:** preserve the preexisting registry; wait for the actual IME window and STOPPED Activity state. Native logs demonstrated the old immediate Home/resume check never reached STOPPED. No test timeout was increased; production lifecycle/draft policies are unchanged. - **Limits:** Fold/resize geometry remains covered by the existing Compose/geometry tests, not a physical foldable-device run. No physical-device or live-Gateway compatibility claim. Earlier local software-AVD startup failed before picker gestures; accelerated installed-app proof now supersedes that execution gap. - **Previous-head CI:** [Ready-state run 36329992179](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36329992179) reached the Play unit job’s 20-minute cap. No OOM or assertion failure was recorded; the exact blocked test is unknown. An isolated replay with matching Android inputs, Temurin 21.0.12.1+1 and the same two-fork policy passed all 3,528 Play and 13 Wear-shared cases in 3m 15s. This does not establish a CI fix; no timeout or worker policy was changed. The picker suite passed in 9.210 s locally and 9.043 s in sibling third-party CI. ### Before / After Same 480 × 800 native Compose window, dark theme, and 30 identical synthetic offline Gateways. Both stills show the result of the same downward touch sequence. The short replay is captured from actual pointer down/move/up frames, slowed for inspection, with captions added outside the application viewport. It is explicitly labeled Robolectric, not device footage.
